key_insight: Agrivoltaic systems can satisfy flexible interconnection export limits not just by curtailing power, but by re-optimizing panel tilt to preserve energy production while improving crop access to sunlight.
engineering_relevance: This shows flexible interconnection agreements can be paired with control strategies that turn curtailment constraints into a co-optimization opportunity for PV generation and agricultural performance.
method: Formulated a seasonal optimization problem for single-axis tracking agrivoltaics.
Optimized time-varying tilt to maximize PV energy while enforcing a real power export limit.
Used the resulting operating schedules to assess both PV output and crop-yield implications.
evidence_signal: A case study over a growing season evaluates the optimized schedules and shows agrivoltaic systems can comply with export limits while improving crop yield.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate seasonal optimization and site-specific assumptions, so real-world performance may vary with weather, crop type, tracker hardware, and interconnection rules.
paper_title: Productive Curtailment in Agrivoltaic Systems under Flexible Interconnection Agreements
